special - Six Canadian Young Men's Christian Association university 
students are looking forward to an International Cooperation 
Year summer different from one which most of their colleagues will have 
back home. These six volunteers will ive their time and talents to the 
World Alliance of YMCAs and the United Nations Relief and Works Azency. 
They will conduct summer programs under the auspices of the Middle “ast 
YMCA Leadership Trainin: Centre, with services to refugees in Jordan, 
Lebanon and the Gaza Strip. 
The six Canadian YMCA volunteers are: {.J.Ellison (\’est Vancouver YMCA); 
J.Henderson (Vancouver Central YMCA); M.C.Luft (University of Alberta- 
Edmonton and Calgary YMCA); D.G.Peden (Victoria YMCA-YWCA); C.M.Shields 
(South Vancouver YMCA); and J.H.C. Soule (!iontreal Lachine-Dorval YMCA and 
Sudbury YiCA). 
"Canada can boast of no greater ambassadors than these", W.Harold Rea, 
Toronto, president of the National Council of YMCAs, commented on the 
announcement of the selection made by M.f.Stronz,/{ontreal,Chairman, 
National YMCA World Service Committee. "orld Service of this kind has 


brought great credit to the YMCA and respect abroad for the name of Canada", 


Mir. Rea added. Elizible candidates were proposed from Ys across Canada 
through YMCA World Service as a project for International Cooperation 
Year. 
This Canadian YMCA - International Cooperation Year (1965) project involves 
the World Alliance of YMNCAs and the United Nations Relief and Works Agency. 
It is a development of the 1961 exnerience of R.D.Sallery (liontreal, now 
Youth Activities Officer, UNRWA Headquarters, Museitbeh Quarter, Beirut, 
Lebanon), J.G.Anderson (North Toronto, now Regina 'Y' Youth Work Secretary ) 
and N.J.Grigzs (Vancouver, student UBC), M.A.Horn (Saskatoon, now 
Assistant Secretary, Montreal Lachine-Dorval 'Y') and 2,A.Patten (Montreal 
student Sir George Williams University) who were 196); volunteers.
